findings.summary: Family (i)'s copula guard is nearly empty, and matching per line misfires both ways on paragraph-length lines; real feature wording still matches
findings.evidence: Family (i) counts an error word as a cue when any copula (is, are, was, were, be, been) is anywhere on the same line. Almost every sentence has a copula, so the guard that round 5 says fixes finding 1 does very little. Real feature wording in this repo still matches. CHANGELOG.md:311 `... is flagged when stale or covering` has stale plus is and no creation or change word. CHANGELOG.md:3076 `whose base is behind is stale until re-verified` is the same. A plausible gate request, `Refuse a push when the head SHA is wrong`, also matches. The unit is also wrong. Requests often put several sentences on one line (the corpus retry request at refusal_corpus.rs:349 has two; steward and user paragraphs are long single lines). So 'same line' is close to 'same paragraph'. That cuts both ways. The exemption fires on any `new` or `add` anywhere in the paragraph, so a real report such as `The decisions page still lists new proposals after they are rejected` is exempt, because `new` is a creation word. Meanwhile the copula branch fires on almost any paragraph that holds stale or wrong. The plan cannot measure the replay share, and its own risk 1 puts that share near the 10% hold. This is the guard that decides whether the job passes verification. Fix: Match cues per sentence, not per line: split on line breaks and on `.`, `;`, `!` or `?` followed by white space. In family (i), require the error word to come right after a copula or `looks`/`seems` (`is wrong`, `are stale`, `looks broken`), or to share a sentence with an output noun. Drop the 'any copula on the line' branch. Apply the creation/change exemption only when that word is the sentence's leading verb (the first token after any bullet marker), so `new proposals` does not exempt a bug report. Add corpus accept cases built from the wording at CHANGELOG.md:311 and 3076 and from `Refuse a push when the head SHA is wrong`. Add a refuse case for `The decisions page still lists new proposals after they are rejected`, and a refuse case with two sentences on one line where the cue sentence has no creation word.
findings.location: Plan decisions 4 and step 2 (family (i) copula guard; creation/change-word exemption; the per-line cue unit)

findings.summary: Family (ii) matches the repo's common 'Fix newcomer gaps on the X page' shape, and no corpus case decides it
findings.evidence: HISTORY.txt holds real subjects of this shape: 685 `Fix newcomer-rated gaps on the firstmate study site page`, 795 `Fix firstmate study page newcomer gaps`, 1496 `Fix six open newcomer findings on the firstmate explainer page`. Family (ii) matches all three because it has fix plus page or site. These are editorial gap fixes from reviewer findings, not wrong-output reports. If their class is code, they would need a root-cause criterion with a code location and a real-data test that fails on the base. Meanwhile HISTORY.txt:115 `Fix firstmate study Reopened state`, a real bug, has no output noun and is not matched. Fix: Decide on purpose whether `Fix <findings/gaps> on the <X> page` is in scope. Add a corpus case (accept or refuse) built from HISTORY.txt:685/1496 with its source named. If it should be accepted, exclude fix lines whose object is findings, gaps or typos.
findings.location: Plan decision 4, family (ii) (fix + output noun) and the corpus in step 7

findings.summary: Whether the cited class is caught depends on the opening verb ('Show only' is caught, 'Make ... show only' is not), and the doc comment does not say so
findings.evidence: `Show only open, above-limit proposals on the decisions page` (HISTORY.txt:13) is refused. `Make the decisions page show only open, above-limit proposals` and `Change the decisions page to list only open proposals` are exempt, because make and change are change words, and the plan pins the first as a non-cue. `The decisions page should list only ...` is a stated gap. So three of four natural phrasings of the t4qv request pass the gate. The doc comment lists `should list only` as a gap but not the make/change phrasings. Fix: Name in the doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry that make/change phrasings of wanted-content requests are not caught. Or narrow the change-word exemption so it does not apply when the line also holds `only` together with still, no longer or anymore, and add a refuse case for `Make the decisions page show only open, above-limit proposals`.
findings.location: Plan decision 4, family (iii) and the 'Make the status page show only running jobs' accept case

summary: The plan puts the fix in the right place: a new `step!` in `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3119-3144), modelled on `check_code_survey` (3453). It passes the retried attempt's request so `try again on <id>` is covered. Its demonstrations use real seams: the corpus `run`/`refusing_check`, `check_root_cause_criterion` called directly, `check_reading_text`, and `include_str!` source and changelog checks like `code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended` (8197). The refuse cases would fail on the base tree. The dependents list matches what I found. `check_design_existing_code` and the gate checks are read only by reading.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, briefs.rs and CHANGELOG.md. The steward re-check (steward.rs:402) and `check_reading_text` (3672) both go through `check_reading_acceptance`. The replay (`replay_cases`, 3759) passes the request only. `READING_RULES` is in the reader brief, not the reader budget set (athena-context lib.rs:280-282). The size and count assertions in briefs.rs (3959-3984) are correctly scheduled for update. The replay-share open question is real and correctly left to the user. The remaining problem is soundness in the cue classifier. Family (i)'s copula guard barely constrains anything because nearly every sentence has a copula. Matching per line, when requests put whole paragraphs on one line, makes both the copula branch and the creation-word exemption (which includes the adjective `new`) misfire. So the round-5 claim that finding 1 is fixed does not hold for real wording in CHANGELOG.md (311, 3076). Since the replay hold decides whether the job passes, this needs tightening: per-sentence matching, a copula right before the error word, and the exemption only for a sentence's leading verb. Then the plan can be accepted.
